title: Double-Verify & Staged-Recovery Protocol
author: Peter Higgins (human authorship for claims); AI-assisted per HUF-STD-001
one_line: Lose nothing; check everything; verify before and after; move slowly in reversible stages; recover from any mistake (AI or human).
lineage: Built over many sessions by the HUF AI Collective caretakers (ChatGPT, Grok, Claude) under Peter; DVR-1.0 names and extends what they built.

four_pillars.lose_nothing: Never delete in place; move superseded material to a dated reversible archive (_archive_YYYY-MM-DD/, _legacy_*) with a manifest. A mistake is always undoable by moving a file back.
four_pillars.double_verify: Every change has a pre-condition check (ground truth before acting) and a post-condition check (it landed as intended after). One check is a guess; two checks are control.
four_pillars.slow_staged: Small, independently verifiable, independently reversible stages, with a human gate between substantive stages (Peter is the sole commit/contact gate).
four_pillars.recovery: Because nothing is deleted and every stage is double-checked, any AI or human mistake is caught at the next gate and rolled back. Recovery is the design.

double_verify_gate.after: read the result back (authoritative); never trust a single bash read of a just-edited file

double_verify_gate.before: confirm move list excludes anything current
double_verify_gate.after: count source+dest, write manifest, confirm reversibility
self-test PASS + clean-data hash unchanged where hash-neutral intended

double_verify_gate.before: PUSH_PROTOCOL §2 (consistency checker, NO-CREATE absent, frozen oracle untouched, JSON parse, self-test)
double_verify_gate.after: §6 closure check: live SHA == recorded SHA, CI green, admin chain rolled

double_verify_gate.before: list what the verification config (CI, checkers) references
double_verify_gate.after: update the verification config to track current files; re-verify

known_failure_modes.what: sandbox mount serves a stale/truncated/NUL-padded copy of a just-written file; bash can falsely report it broken or show the OLD code's line numbers in a traceback
known_failure_modes.authority: Read/Write/Edit tools are authoritative (Windows-side); bash reads can lag
known_failure_modes.recovery: verify via the authoritative Read tool; reconstruct to /tmp to run; validate big admin JSONs Windows-side; never blind-edit them from the sandbox

known_failure_modes.id: FM-2 stale pipeline / verification coupled to moved files
known_failure_modes.what: CI/checkers hard-wired to old paths fail when structure changes (validate.yml checked for + ran the archived tools/pipeline)
known_failure_modes.recovery: treat the verification config as part of the structure; update the checker's file list in the same change; a red here is the system catching drift loudly

known_failure_modes.what: narrating a commit you have not seen corrupts the audit trail
known_failure_modes.recovery: never fabricate; use placeholders, flag the blocker, reconcile at the human gate (honest-broker applied to bookkeeping)

known_failure_modes.what: push numbers and CI runs desync; empty-and-repaste can skip chain entries
known_failure_modes.recovery: §6 closure check reconciles at the gate; draft control rows number-agnostically until confirmed

known_failure_modes.what: anyone can make a wrong call
known_failure_modes.recovery: before/after double-check catches it at the next gate; reversibility undoes it. No single actor trusted to be right once; the system is trusted to catch it twice.

design_claim.statement: DVR applies the engine's epistemology (determinism + hash receipts: same input -> same output -> same content hash) to the operations layer: every state has a checkable receipt before and after, plus a reversible path back. That is why the system absorbs a buffered read, a stale pipeline, a mis-numbered push, or a plain mistake without losing anything.
